title: Affine-test relative dualizing trace pairs
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Y$ be a scheme over $S$, and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Regard $Y$ as its represented algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] and fix $f:X\to Y$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the full subcategories with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use the canonical small-etale module calculus [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus], derived tensor pullback and its identity and composition comparisons [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback], the counit-mate exchange $\beta:La^*Rf_*\to Rf'_*Lp^*$ [def-sfb-space-module-derived-exchange], the normalized affine derived-section and structure-object comparisons [def-sfb-space-affine-sections-compositors], and the canonical structure pullback $La^*\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal O_{Y'}$: the map adjoint, under the derived pullback--pushforward adjunction [def-sfb-space-affine-hom-comparison], to the regular-function structure map $\mathcal O_{Y'}\to a_*\mathcal O$ [def-sfb-space-module-structure-map], taken on the small models [def-sfb-space-small-ringed-model] through the module direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], placed in degree zero and followed by the universal right-derived unit to $Ra_*$. A trace pair is $(K,t)$ with $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $t:Rf_*K\to\mathcal O_Y$. An isomorphism of trace pairs $e:(K,t)\to(L,s)$ satisfies $s\circ Rf_*e=t$. In a commuting scheme-base square, an isomorphism $e:Lp^*K\to K'$ is trace compatible when $t'\circ Rf'_*e\circ\beta_K=(La^*t)$ followed by the canonical structure pullback. The affine-test dualizing property says that $K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and, for every affine $a:Y'\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ and every cartesian realization $X'$ of $X\times_YY'$, there exists a trace $t':Rf'_*Lp^*K\to\mathcal O_{Y'}$ trace compatible with $(K,t)$ and the identity on $Lp^*K$, such that for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'})$ composition with $t'$, followed by the normalized derived-section comparisons, gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_{X'})}(E,Lp^*K)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(R\Gamma(X',E),A[0])$. These maps are natural in $E$ by their composition formula. On proper flat finitely presented morphisms this is the relative dualizing complex condition of Tag 0E5X; the first remark there permits omission of relative perfectness from this defining property.
